Congressman Miller’s Health Advisory Council sounds like another layer of bureaucracy masquerading as a solution. Advisory councils often become taxpayer-funded talking shops—endless meetings, zero accountability. The Erie County Health Department’s District Advisory Council, for example, exists to “make recommendations” but has no authority to enforce real change.

If this new council isn’t tied to specific legislative action—like defunding bloated programs or redirecting resources to patient care—it’s just more D.C. theater. Healthcare needs fewer committees and more reforms: slash pharma price-gouging, audit Medicare fraud, and let states—not federal appointees—drive innovation.

Otherwise, it’s all optics, no results.
